question.worked_solution:
First, recall that:

$$
{lim}_{t\to 3}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}({t}^{2}-3t) \\ {lim}_{t\to 3}\frac{1}{{t}^{2}-8} \\ {lim}_{t\to 3}(5-2t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

- For the first component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}({t}^{2}-3t) & ={3}^{2}-3(3)=0\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}\frac{1}{{t}^{2}-8} & =\frac{1}{{3}^{2}-8}=1\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}(5-2t) & =5-2(3)=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{t\to 3}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the limit of $‖f(t)‖$ as $t$ approaches $3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 3}‖f(t)‖ & =‖{lim}_{t\to 3}f(t)‖ \\  & =‖[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
